summary: 单调街景可能使行人失去注意力。研究者用街头实验考察建筑立面的复杂度、敬畏感与互助行为，说明街道需要持续提供适度的新鲜感，同时避免信息过载。

paragraphs.brief: 人们认为，在复杂的环境中，而不是在“大、空、空的办公室”中，发挥最佳功能。
sentences: A growing body of research in cognitive science illuminates the physical and mental toll bland cityscapes take on residents.
越来越多的认知科学研究照亮了居民在身心上遭受的伤害
Generally, these researchers argue that humans are healthier when they live surrounded by variety or work in well-designed, unique spaces, rather than unattractive, generic ones.
一般而言，这些研究人员认为，人类在多样化的周围生活或工作于设计完善的独特空间，而不是不吸引人的普通空间，是更健康的。

Urban policy professor Justin Hollander and architect Ann Sussman review scientific data to help architects and urban planners understand how, exactly, people respond to their built surroundings, particularly at work.
城市政策教授Justin Hollander和建筑师Ann Sussman 审查了科学数据，以帮助建筑师和城市规划者了解人们如何确切地应对其建筑环境，特别是在工作场所。
People, they argue, function best in intricate settings, not ‘big, blank, boxy offices’.
人们认为，在复杂的环境中，而不是在“大、空、空的办公室”中，发挥最佳功能。

paragraphs.brief: 艾拉德解释说，城市设计的主要目标应该是每隔几秒钟就产生某种新颖或变化；否则，我们就会在认知上脱离。
sentences: Indeed, that’s what Colin Ellard, a neuroscientist at the University of Waterloo in Canada, has found in his work.
事实上，加拿大滑铁卢大学神经科学家科林·埃拉德在他的著作中发现了这一点。
Five years ago, Ellard became interested in a certain building—the gigantic Whole Foods Market ‘plopped into’ a notoriously textured part of Lower Manhattan in New York.
五年前，艾拉德开始对一座建筑感兴趣，这座巨大的全食品市场“陷入了纽约曼哈顿下游一个臭名昭著的纹身区。

Ellard partnered with the Guggenheim Museum to analyze what happens when someone walks out of a tiny neighborhood restaurant and encounters a full city block with nothing but ‘the long, blank facade of the Whole Foods Market building’.
埃拉德与古根海姆博物馆合作，研究这样一种体验：一个人从街区里的小餐馆走出来，眼前的整个街区只有全食超市大楼那面“漫长而空白的外墙”，此时他会有什么反应？
In 2011, Ellard led small groups on Lower East Side walks to measure the effect of the urban environment on them.
2011年，Ellard带领下东区小团体步行，衡量城市环境对他们的影响。
Participants recorded their responses to questions at each stopping point and wore sensors that measured skin conductance, a response to emotional excitement.
参加者记录了他们在每个停留点对问题的答复，并携带了测量皮肤导体的传感器，这是对情绪激动的一种反应。
Passing the monolithic Whole Foods Market, people’s state of arousal plummeted.
整个食品市场一团糟，人们的情绪暴跌。
Physiologically, Ellard explained, they were bored.
从生理学上说，艾拉德解释说，他们很无聊。
To describe this place, they used words like ‘bland’ and ‘passionless’.
他们用“bland”和“belion”等字眼描述这个地方。

In contrast, one block east at the other test site—‘a lively sea of restaurants with lots of open doors and windows’—people measured high levels of excitement, and they listed words like ‘lively’ and ‘socializing’.
相反，在另一个试验场的东面的一个街区—— “充满活力的餐馆，有很多开着的门和窗子”—— 人们测量到兴奋程度很高，他们列出了“活的”和“社会化”等词。
Ellard explains that the main objective of urban design should be to produce some kind of novelty or change every few seconds; otherwise, we become cognitively disengaged.
艾拉德解释说，城市设计的主要目标应该是每隔几秒钟就产生某种新颖或变化；否则，我们就会在认知上脱离。

paragraphs.brief: 其技巧似乎是设计一个令人兴奋但不会给我们的功能带来大量信息的世界
sentences: The trick, it seems, is to design a world that excites but doesn’t overload our faculties with a constant barrage of information.
其技巧似乎是设计一个令人兴奋但不会给我们的功能带来大量信息的世界
‘We are, as animals, programmed to respond to thrill,’ said professor Brendan Walker.
布伦登·沃克教授说，`我们作为动物，被编程用来应对激动。

In Walker’s ‘thrill laboratory’ at the University of Nottingham in the UK, devices measure heart rate and skin conductance to see how people respond to adrenaline-producing experiences such as a roller-coaster ride.
在英国诺丁汉大学的沃克`Thrill实验室 ' 中，装置测量心率和皮肤导体，以观察人们如何应对滚车车等肾上腺素生成的经历。
A thrilling encounter moves us quickly from a state of equilibrium to a desirable ‘disorientation’.
令人兴奋的遭遇很快地将我们从一个平衡状态变为一个理想的“偏向”。
‘Humans want a certain element of turmoil or confusion,’ he said.
他说：人类想要某种混乱或混乱的因素。
‘Complexity is thrilling whether in an amusement park or architecture.’
复杂是令人兴奋的无论是在游乐公园还是建筑。

paragraphs.brief: 心理学家发现敬畏的时刻可以改善我们的福祉。
sentences: Psychologists have found that awe-inspiring moments can potentially improve our well-being.
心理学家发现敬畏的时刻可以改善我们的福祉。
One study conducted by Melanie Rudd, Kathleen Vohs and Jennifer Aaker of Stanford University in the US showed that the feeling of ‘awe’ can make people more patient and less materialistic.
由美国斯坦福大学的Melanie Rudd、Kathleen Vohs和Jennifer Aaker进行的一项研究表明，“敬畏”的感觉可以使人们更加耐心，减少物质主义。
In an experiment, the researchers showed students 60-second clips of waterfalls, whales, or astronauts in space.
在一次实验中，研究人员向学生展示了60秒的瀑布、鲸鱼或太空人。
After only a minute of virtual images, those who said they were awed also felt less pressed for time.
说自己已入睡的人，对于自己已逝去的岁月，也感到压力不大：“仅经过一分钟的虚拟图像。”
And in another variation, people made hypothetical choices between physical and experiential goods of equal monetary value.
在另一种变化中，人们在物质和实验品之间做出了同样的货币价值的假设选择。
Those who had just ‘felt awe’ were more likely to choose an experience over a possession, a choice that is linked with greater satisfaction in the long run.
那些刚刚“敬畏”的人更可能选择一种经验而不是占有，而从长远来看，这种选择与更满意联系在一起。
In other words, a visual buzz—whether architectural or natural—might have the ability to change our frame of mind, making modern-day life more satisfying and interactive.
换句话说，视觉的嗡嗡声——无论是建筑上的还是自然的——可能有能力改变我们的思维框架，使现代生活更加令人满意和互动。

paragraphs.brief: 在接受援助的人中，在活跃地点提供使用电话的人数是他们的7倍。
sentences: It’s important to note, however, that architectural boredom isn’t about how pristine a street is.
但重要的是要指出，建筑上的无聊并不是关于街道的纯净性。
People often confuse successful architecture with whether an area looks pleasant.
人们常常混淆成功的建筑与一个区域是否看起来愉快。
On the contrary, when it comes to city buildings, people often focus too narrowly on aesthetics, said Charles Montgomery, author of Happy City: Transforming Our Lives Through Urban Design.
相反，在城市建筑方面，人们往往过于狭隘地关注美学，这是《快乐城市：通过城市设计改变我们的生活》的作者Charles Montgomery说的。
Some of the happiest blocks in New York City, he argues, are ‘kind of ugly and messy’.
他说，纽约市一些最开心的街区有点丑陋和混乱
In 2014, Montgomery’s Happy City Lab conducted an experiment in which he found a strong correlation between messier blocks and pro-social behavior.
2014年，蒙哥马利的快乐城市实验室进行了一项实验，发现更混乱的街区与亲社会行为之间有着密切的关联。
Montgomery sent researchers, posing as lost tourists, to places he coded as either ‘active’ or ‘inactive’ facades.
Montgomery派遣研究人员，假扮为失落的游客，前往他认为「积极」或「不活跃」的地方。
He concluded that the former had a high level of interest—that is, they were messy—while the latter had no special features such as long warehouse blocks.
他最后说，前者具有很高的兴趣，即它们很混乱，而后者没有长仓库区块等特殊特征。
Pedestrians at active sites were nearly five times more likely to offer assistance than at inactive ones.
活跃地点的行人提供援助的可能性比不活跃地点几乎高出五倍。
Of those who assisted, seven times as many at the active site offered use of their phones.
在接受援助的人中，在活跃地点提供使用电话的人数是他们的7倍。

paragraphs.brief: 乘坐曼哈顿中城的2006年赫斯特塔
sentences: Fortunately, it’s not necessarily a dichotomy—new architecture can achieve the optimal level of cacophony and beauty.
幸运的是，它不一定是两极分化的，新的建筑可以达到最佳的恋情和美。
Take the 2006 Hearst Tower in midtown Manhattan.
乘坐曼哈顿中城的2006年赫斯特塔
Designed by architect Norman Foster, Hearst Tower is a glass-and-steel skyscraper, 40 stories of which are designed in a triangular pattern, differing in style from the 1920s Art Deco base.
赫斯特塔是由建筑师诺曼·福斯特设计的，是一个玻璃和钢铁摩天大楼，其40个故事是用三角模式设计的，风格与1920年代的艺术Deco基地不同。
From the outside, the facade jolts city dwellers from their daily commutes, while energizing employees who enter it each morning.
外表的外表让城市居民每天的通勤感到震撼，同时也激励员工们每天早上都来上班。
For many who walk by, Hearst Tower’s design may not be the easiest to understand; it’s both sleek and old.
对于许多路过的人来说，赫斯特塔的设计也许不是最容易理解的，它既流露又老。
The top looks like it traveled from the future.
顶部看起来是来自未来
Inside, workers travel upon diagonal escalators, up a three-story water sculpture, through the tower’s historic atrium, flooded with light.
工人们乘坐双层扶梯，爬上一座三层水雕塑，穿过这座塔上的历史阁楼，满是光线。
Few New Yorkers who pass by would find this building boring.
很少有经过纽约的人会发现这栋楼很无聊
And they’re likely to be happier—maybe even nicer to each other—because of it.
他们可能会更快乐 - 也许对彼此更好 - 因为这。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 题干问“正面影响”,F段描述赫斯特大厦对路人和员工的积极情绪与行为影响，完全对应。
回到对应内容“外表的外表让城市居民每天的通勤感到震撼，同时也激励员工们每天早上都来上班”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: Ellard explains … ; otherwise, we become cognitively disengaged.
“that the main objective of urban design should be to produce some kind of novelty or change every few seconds”补足 explains 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 explains 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
Those … ’ were more likely to choose an experience over a possession, a choice that is linked with greater satisfaction in the long run.
“who had just ‘felt awe”修饰前面的 Those。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 Those，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: There could be more than an economic or nostalgic price to impersonal retail and high-rise construction; boring architecture may take an emotional toll on the people forced to live with it.
对非个人性零售和高楼建筑来说，可能不止是经济或怀旧价格；无聊的建筑可能会给被迫与之生活在一起的人带来情感上的伤害。
